commons:31786023.summary: In the half-dome of the apse the Virgin stands on a footstool against a gold ground, holding the Christ Child on her left arm, between two archangels in white robes who bear sceptres and offer orbs. The inscription above her reads HAGIA MARIA, and a decorative border runs along the base of the conch. Surviving from an early Christian basilica and built into the later church, it is one of the finest early Byzantine wall mosaics in Cyprus and a rare survivor of the age before Iconoclasm.
facts: The apse of a 5th-century basilica, with its 6th-century mosaic, was incorporated into the later Byzantine church (11th century), which is why the mosaic survived the basilica's destruction.
The Virgin is labelled HAGIA MARIA ('Holy Mary') rather than Theotokos; the archangels' wings are rendered like peacock feathers, and the border shows a Fountain of Life with ducks, parrots and deer.
The church was placed on Cyprus's tentative list for UNESCO World Heritage in 2015.
commons:31786023.notes: Dated on stylistic grounds (Megaw) to the 6th century, probably its later part; some writers date it to the 7th. The photograph shows the whole apse at a distance.

cur:objects-khanenko-john-the-baptist-ic.summary: St John the Baptist, gaunt and long-haired, stands in his camel-hair garment and points with his right hand, the gesture of the Forerunner who announces the Lamb of God. In the upper corners two small medallions show Christ and the Virgin, toward whom John's witness is directed. Though worn, the icon keeps the spiritual intensity of the earliest Byzantine panel paintings.
facts: Wikipedia lists 'John the Baptist' (6th century) among the four early Byzantine 'Sinai' icons of the Khanenko Museum, acquired in 1940.
cur:objects-khanenko-john-the-baptist-ic.notes: The medallions are small and worn in the available image; their identification as Christ (left) and the Virgin (right) follows the usual description of the icon. Image is small (436 px).
